headline: Democrats took Congress, stocks ripped, and the Fed is still leaning toward another hike.
regime: Hiking regime: the Fed raised rates in September and traders put roughly 70-85% odds on another 25bp hike on Dec 9. In this regime good economic news can be bad for stocks, and yields matter more than usual.

lean.t: Choppy after a big gap day
lean.why: Wednesday was a relief rally (SPY +1.65%). Thursday has only minor data (layoff counts, productivity), and everyone is waiting on Friday's jobs report. Trade levels, do not chase gaps.

lean.t: Slight upward lean, hinges on jobs and CPI
lean.why: A hike is mostly priced in, so a soft jobs or CPI print that cools hike odds is the bullish surprise. A hot print pushes the 10-year back over 5% and hurts rate-sensitive groups.

Stocks have risen in the 12 months after every midterm since 1950, and gridlock limits big new laws. The offsets: AI spending is under political scrutiny and the Nasdaq-100 just fell 10% from its early-October high.

rates.n: Held Oct 28, 10-2 vote; Cook and Hammack wanted a hike
Kalshi 72%, CME and Reuters about 81-82%, Bloomberg about 85%
Fell about 5-6bp on the election, was back above 5% on Fed day
Freddie Mac survey of Oct 22, down 8bp from 7.40%
Slid on the election day move

sectors.why: Democratic control keeps federal clean-energy support alive. First Solar +9%, Sunrun +10%, Enphase +8% premarket. Gridlock caps new laws, and spikes like this often give back some of the gain.
Democrats favor more health spending. Centene +4.5%, Molina +6%, HCA +3.7% premarket. UnitedHealth fell, so this is a stock-picker's group.
Northrop -5%, RTX, Lockheed and L3Harris about -3%. The hoped-for $1.5T budget could come in lower. Defense budgets have usually been bipartisan, so deep cuts are less likely than headlines suggest.

The most exposed theme: public opposition to nearby data centers rose from 28% to about half of Americans, and hearings are more likely. Nasdaq-100 is in a 10% correction but still holds its 200-day average.
Hikes widen lending margins, but Democrats mean more scrutiny and credit risk if jobs weaken. JPMorgan, BofA and Goldman all reported strong Q3s.
Mortgage rates follow the 10-year, which sits near 4.9%, so 30-year loans stay above 7%. A fall in the 10-year is the only fast fix.
A weaker dollar and lower yields helped, and Capital Economics says the Democratic sweep raised worries about the fiscal outlook. After a 3% day, wait for pullbacks to the $4,000 area.
Oil slid and WTI sits near $94. Lower oil helps airlines and shippers and hurts drillers.
Small caps finished lower on Fed day because they borrow short. They are the most sensitive to hike odds, for better or worse.
Tesla -3.6%, SpaceX -3.2%, Trump Media -7% on the election. Trump Media is one of our day-trade picks, so size it small.
They trade like bonds. A falling 10-year helps them, a spike over 5% hurts them.
GEO -6.7% and CoreCivic -5.2%. Both had rallied on the immigration crackdown that a new Congress could oversee.

news.head: Fed holds at 3.75-4.00%, but two officials voted to hike
news.mean: It was a 10-2 vote, up from 12-0 in September. The Fed upgraded growth from 'solid' to 'strong' and dropped language about steering inflation back to 2%. Chair Warsh said politics played no role. The signal is that the next move is more likely up than down.
react: Bond proxies lose when yields rise
Small caps closed lower on Fed day
news.hist: In the last three hiking cycles, JPMorgan rose in all three (+22.6%, +57.7%, +16.8%). Bank of America fell 24.8% in 2022-23, so 'banks win when rates rise' is not automatic.
news.today: Do not bet against the 10-year. If it pushes back over 5%, rate-sensitive groups (homebuilders, REITs, small caps) get hit first.
news.later: Quality banks with the strongest track record in hiking cycles are the cleanest way to invest in higher rates. Watch for the hiking cycle to end, which has often been when growth stocks recover.

news.head: 30-year mortgage rate: 7.32%, still above 7%
news.mean: Mortgage rates track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the Fed funds rate. The 10-year near 4.9% keeps 30-year loans above 7%. Fannie Mae and the MBA had forecast 6.7-6.8% by Q2 2027, but that was before September's hike, so treat it as stale. A newer weekly survey may already be out.
react: Owners locked into low rates stay put
news.hist: Rule of thumb: homebuilder stocks often move before sales numbers do, rallying when the 10-year turns down and sinking when it breaks higher.
news.today: Trade homebuilders off the 10-year chart, not off housing news. 10-year up means builders down.
news.later: A housing recovery needs the 30-year sustained below about 6.5%. Start accumulating builders only after the 10-year clearly rolls over.

news.head: Democrats win Congress: stocks surge, gridlock is the base case
news.mean: The Dow rose more than 1,200 points (+2.4%) early, and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq gained 1.7% and 2.1%. Capital Economics and Wells Fargo both say they do not expect sweeping policy changes. Democrats lack a filibuster-proof Senate and the president can veto.
react: Uncertainty is gone, gridlock limits new taxes and spending
Fewer unfunded tax cuts means a smaller deficit, so yields eased
Moves are repricing risk, not actual law changes
news.hist: Per Edward Jones, the S&P 500 rose an average 15.5% in the six months after the last 14 midterms (since 1970). Another analysis found it higher 12 months after all 19 midterms since 1950, averaging about 15%.
news.today: After a +1.7% gap day, wait for a pullback to yesterday's range rather than buying the first green candle.
news.later: History favors owning stocks through the next 6-12 months. Averages hide big drawdowns on the way, so scale in.

news.head: Clean energy leads the post-election rally
news.mean: Democratic control could keep federal clean-energy support in place and speed approvals. First Solar +9.4%, Sunrun +10%, Enphase +7.6%, NextEra +2.2%, Vestas about +5%, Orsted about +7%. Tesla was the exception, down 3.6%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: policy-driven spikes often retrace part of the move within weeks if no actual law changes, because gridlock caps the upside too.
news.today: Gap-up leaders are prone to fading. Better entries come on first pullback with volume dropping.
news.later: Own the group through dips only if you believe rates will fall; solar is heavily financed and hates 5% yields.

news.head: Health insurers and hospitals jump
news.mean: Democrats favor more health spending. Centene +4.5%, Molina +6%, HCA +3.7%, Universal Health Services +2.2%. BNP Paribas doubts the Affordable Care Act can be restored in full but expects budget concessions. UnitedHealth fell while HCA rose, so the group is not moving as one.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: healthcare policy hopes have lifted these stocks before and faded when legislation stalled, so watch real bills, not headlines.
news.today: Trade the relative strength of hospitals over insurers, and skip names that are falling on their own news.
news.later: Hospitals and Medicaid insurers benefit most from any coverage expansion; wait for earnings to confirm.

news.head: Defense stocks drop on budget worries
news.mean: Northrop Grumman fell 5%, and RTX, Lockheed Martin and L3Harris each fell over 3%. Support had partly rested on an expected $1.5T budget request that a Democratic Congress could leave short.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: defense budgets have historically passed with support from both parties, so cuts are usually smaller than first feared.
news.today: Gap-down names can bounce; trade the reclaim of yesterday's close, not the first dip.
news.later: Long-term buyers can use weakness in prime contractors, but a lower budget request is a real headwind for the next year.

news.head: AI chips wobble on data-center regulation fears
news.mean: Chip stocks first fell on concerns about tighter data center regulation, and the Nasdaq-100 entered a correction (down 10% from its early-October high), closing just above its 200-day moving average. AMD beat estimates but slipped after an early rally. Super Micro rose on strong results.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: the 200-day average is the line many traders watch. Schwab noted the Nasdaq-100 closed just above it after falling 10% from its high.
news.today: Trade the Nasdaq-100 200-day line: hold = bounce plays in leaders, break = stand aside.
news.later: AI spending is still the main growth engine. Opposition to data centers is a risk to build-out speed, not to demand.

news.head: Gold back above $4,000 as the dollar sinks
news.mean: Gold rose about 3% to just above $4,040. The dollar index fell about 0.6% to 101.27, a 1-month low, the 10-year fell about 5bp to near 4.9%, silver rose 4.8% to $52.13. A weaker dollar and lower yields both make gold more attractive.
news.hist: Gold usually rises when the dollar and real yields fall. The risk is the Fed: a hot jobs or CPI print lifts hike odds, which can reverse all of it.
news.today: A 3% day invites a pullback. Look for a retest of $4,000 that holds.
news.later: Fiscal worries and a weaker dollar are slow-burn supports; scale in on dips instead of at the highs.

news.head: Oil slides after the election
news.mean: WTI sat near $93.71 and the Nov 4 FXStreet headline reads 'Oil plunges'. Lower oil lowers input costs and helps inflation, which can ease hike odds at the margin.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: oil swings of this size feed through to CPI within a month or two, which is why the Nov 10 CPI matters for oil-sensitive sectors.
news.today: Pairs idea: airlines up, energy down while oil is falling. Stop out if oil reverses.
news.later: Do not invest on one down day. Wait for a trend.

news.head: October jobs report Friday: the market's next big test
news.mean: Consensus is +65k jobs (range 35k to 125k), unemployment 4.2%, and wages +2.9% year over year (+0.3% month over month). September was only +29k. ADP showed +86k private jobs for October. In a hiking regime, strong data raises hike odds and yields.
react: Yields up, stocks mixed to lower, dollar up
Yields down, hike odds fall, growth and small caps rally
Strong jobs helps credit, weak jobs lowers rates
news.hist: Rule of thumb: when the Fed is hiking, the market often reacts to the rate path first and the economy second, so 'good news is bad news' trades can appear.
news.today: Avoid holding big day trades into 8:30 ET Friday. Look for the second 15 minutes after the number for direction.
news.later: A string of weak reports would end the hiking story and start a different one: slowdown risk. That changes which sectors lead.

news.head: Inflation: CPI lands Nov 10, and hike odds hang on it
news.mean: BofA projects CPI inflation of 3.3% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, well above the Fed's 2% goal. The Fed said inflation 'remains elevated'. A cooler CPI could trim hike odds; a hot one would make December close to a lock.
react: Yields up, homebuilders and small caps down, dollar up
Yields down, gold and growth up
Inflation hedges if CPI surprises up
news.hist: Rule of thumb: CPI days are among the most volatile of the month. Core readings matter more than the headline.
news.today: Reduce size into the print. The reaction often reverses within hours.
news.later: Persistent 3%+ inflation argues for pricing power, real assets and short-duration bonds.

news.head: Big banks post strong Q3, but the group has lagged the Fed's hikes
news.mean: JPMorgan Q3 EPS was $5.57 (about 13x forward earnings). Bank of America net interest income rose 8% to $16.45B and a 100bp rise would add about $1.4B. Goldman's EPS of $17.01 beat the $13.65 consensus. Even so, a September report noted the Fed's hike did not lift bank stocks, and banks sold off before Q3 earnings. Democrats may add scrutiny.
react: Largest rate lever but bond-loss risk
news.today: Banks trade with the yield curve and credit headlines. A hot jobs print is mixed: good for loans, bad if it raises recession fears.
news.later: If you want one bank for a hiking cycle, history favors JPMorgan. The main risk to any bank is rising unemployment.

news.head: Musk and Trump-linked stocks fall on the election
news.mean: SpaceX fell 3.2%, Tesla 3.6%, Trump Media 7%. The article also notes a possible slower scrutiny of a SpaceX-Tesla merger. Trump Media is one of the day-trade picks on our Parabolic Movers page, so this is a live example of news hitting a pick.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: stocks tied to a single political outcome are headline-driven and often gap in both directions within days.
news.today: If you trade these, use small size and hard stops; they can gap 10% either way.
news.later: Avoid long-term positions justified only by a political view.

calendar.usual: Minor mover; layoffs rising feeds the 'cold jobs' story ahead of Friday.
Consensus +65k, 4.2%, wages +0.3% m/m. Big moves in yields, dollar and banks.
The key input to December's hike. Core matters more than the headline.
Hike odds are about 70-85%. A hold would be a surprise rally for growth and small caps.

scen.title: What if Friday's jobs number is...

out: Mixed to lower; growth and small caps worst
Relief; focus moves to CPI Nov 10
Growth and small caps rally, unless recession fear takes over

playbook: Homebuilders, REITs, utilities, small caps and unprofitable growth are pressured first. Banks and the dollar hold up better.
Housing, small caps, growth and gold benefit. Mortgage rates ease a few weeks later.
Gold and miners, emerging markets and big multinationals gain. Importers lose.
Airlines, cruise lines and shippers win. Energy stocks lose. Headline inflation eases.
A growth and small-cap rally is the usual response. Banks lose some margin tailwind.
Bonds rally, defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) lead. Cyclicals and banks get hit by recession worries.
